title: The skill gap between using AI and architecting AI.
summary: The post contrasts using AI as a coding tool (prompt engineering, model selection) with architecting real-world AI systems for business (agent orchestration, failure handling, integration patterns). It argues that designing multi-agent systems that integrate with transactional systems requires a fundamentally different skill set than using AI for faster coding.
key_points: Prompt engineering and using AI coding tools is distinct from designing production AI systems that orchestrate multiple agents and handle real business workflows.
Real-world AI architecture requires skills in agent orchestration, failure mode analysis, integration patterns, error classification, async flows, and cost-aware design.
These architectural patterns are learned through shipping systems, observing failures in production, and iterating on structural solutions.
Few people have multi-agent systems architecture expertise despite widespread adoption of AI coding tools, creating a critical skill gap in the industry.

quotes.text: Using AI as a coding tool is not the same as architecting an AI application for a real business problem.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the central distinction that most AI training focuses on tool usage rather than system-level design for production environments.

quotes.text: These aren't tips. They're architectural patterns.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies that successful AI systems require formal design patterns similar to traditional systems architecture, not just best practice tips.
